African National Congress (ANC) is a political party in South Africa.

Alina Kabaeva (or Kabayeva; born 12 May 1983) is a Russian politician, media manager, and retired individual rhythmic gymnast, who has been designated Honoured Master of Sports by the Russian government.

António Costa (born 17 July 1961) is a Portuguese lawyer and politician who has served as president of the European Council since 2024.
This short-lived Dutch state, the first of Napoleonic France's 'sister' client states, ended in 1806 when Louis Bonaparte took the Dutch throne — what was it known as?
Batavian Republic was the successor state to the Republic of the Seven United Netherlands.

Book of Daniel is a 2nd-century BC biblical apocalypse with a 6th-century BC setting.
He argued that all living things descend from a common ancestor, shaped by what he called natural selection — which English naturalist was he?
Charles Darwin (12 February 1809 - 19 April 1882) was an English naturalist, geologist, and biologist, widely known for his contributions to evolutionary biology.
His name means roughly 'Descending Eagle,' and he took the throne of Tenochtitlan in 1520 as the last Aztec emperor while the city lay under Spanish siege. Who was he?
Cuauhtémoc (Nahuatl), also known as Cuauhtemotzn, Guatimozn, or Guatmoc, was the Aztec ruler (tlatoani) of Tenochtitlan from 1520 to 1521, and the last Aztec Emperor.
This Russian diplomat has served as the official spokesman for President Vladimir Putin since 2012 — who is he?
Dmitry Peskov (born 17 October 1967) is a Russian diplomat serving as the spokesman for Russian president Vladimir Putin since 2012.

Erich Hartmann (19 April 1922 - 20 September 1993), nicknamed Bubi, was a German fighter pilot during World War II and the most successful fighter ace in the history of aerial warfare.

Franz Josef Strauss (6 September 1915 - 3 October 1988) was a German politician.

Giuseppe Garibaldi (4 July 1807 - 2 June 1882) was an Italian general, revolutionary and republican.
This Norwegian monarch has reigned since 1991, and as a child during World War II went into exile with his royal family, spending time in Sweden and the United States. Who is he?
Harald V (born 21 February 1937) is King of Norway, having reigned since 17 January 1991.

Possibly originating beyond the Black Sea, this Anatolian Indo-European people built one of the first major Bronze Age civilizations in West Asia, peaking under king Suppiluliuma I from a capital called Hattusa — who were they?

Hittites were an Anatolian Indo-European people who formed one of the first major civilizations of the Bronze Age in West Asia. Scholars once attributed the development of iron-smelting to the Hittites, who were thought to have monopolized ironworking during the Bronze Age.
The son of Abraham and Sarah and father of Jacob and Esau, this patriarch's name means 'he will laugh,' referencing his parents' reaction to news of his birth at their advanced ages — who is he?
Isaac is the second Hebrew patriarch in Judaism and an important figure in the Abrahamic religions, including Samaritanism, Christianity, Islam, the Bah' Faith, and Rastafari.

A lifelong pacifist and the first woman ever elected to U.S. federal office, she opposed entering the First World War — and in 1941 cast the lone congressional vote against declaring war again. Who was she?
Jeannette Rankin (June 11, 1880 - May 18, 1973) was an American politician and women's rights advocate who became the first woman to hold federal office in the United States.
His pivotal role in Hong Kong's 2014 Umbrella Movement landed this teen activist on Time's Most Influential Teens list and a Person of the Year nomination — who is he?
Joshua Wong (Cantonese; born 13 October 1996) is a Hong Kong activist and politician.

Emerging from the breakup of the Western Turkic Khaganate in the late 6th century CE, this semi-nomadic Turkic people built a powerful trading empire spanning parts of modern Russia, Ukraine, and Kazakhstan — who were they?

Khazars (/kzrz/) were a semi-nomadic Turkic people who established a major commercial empire in the late 6th century CE spanning the south of modern European Russia, southern Ukraine, and western Kazakhstan.

An army doctor who earned the Medal of Honor on the frontier, he commanded the Rough Riders with Theodore Roosevelt as his deputy and later became a leading contender for the 1920 presidential nomination. Who was he?
Leonard Wood (October 9, 1860 - August 7, 1927) was a United States Army major general, physician, and public official.

Minoan civilization was a Bronze Age culture which was centered on the island of Crete. Known for its monumental architecture and energetic art, it is often regarded as the first civilization in Europe.
This Indian politician and writer served as Chief Minister of Odisha for over two decades before becoming the state's Leader of Opposition in 2024 — who is he?
Naveen Patnaik (born 16 October 1946) is an Indian politician and writer, who is currently Leader of Opposition in Odisha Legislative Assembly.
As a National Security Council staffer, this retired Marine officer helped orchestrate the arms-for-hostages scheme that fueled a 1980s political scandal — who is he?
Oliver North (born October 7, 1943) is an American political commentator, television host, military historian, author, and retired United States Marine Corps lieutenant colonel.

This Roman emperor, the son of a freed slave, rose through a military career distinguishing himself in the Parthian War before briefly ruling for three months in 193 after Commodus's assassination — who was he?
Pertinax (1 August 126 - 28 March 193) was Roman emperor for the first three months of 193, succeeding Commodus and becoming the first ruler of the turbulent Year of the Five Emperors.
One of the wealthiest Canadians of his era, this New Brunswick-born lawyer made his fortune in a Calgary law partnership before serving as Canada's prime minister from 1930 to 1935 — who was he?
R. B. Bennett (July 3, 1870 - June 26, 1947) was a Canadian lawyer, businessman, philanthropist, and politician who served as the 11th prime minister of Canada from 1930 to 1935.

This Zimbabwean revolutionary served as his country's first prime minister after independence in 1980, then as president until being deposed in a 2017 coup after nearly four decades in power. Who is he?
Robert Mugabe (muu-,; 21 February 1924 - 6 September 2019) was a Zimbabwean revolutionary and politician who led Zimbabwe from 1980 until he was deposed in a coup in 2017.
She led Finland's Social Democrats from 2020 to 2023 and was the country's prime minister before resigning her parliament seat to advise political leaders abroad — who is she?

Sanna Marin (born 16 November 1985) is a Finnish politician who served as prime minister of Finland from 2019 to 2023 and as the leader of the Social Democratic Party of Finland (SDP) from 2020 to 2023.

Smedley Butler (July 30, 1881 - June 21, 1940) was a United States Marine Corps officer.
This form of governance bases decisions on evidence, efficiency, and scientific expertise rather than democratic deliberation — what is it called?
Technocracy is an expert-based type of governance.

One of the few government agencies explicitly authorized by the U.S. Constitution, this independent federal agency began operations in 1971, replacing a former Cabinet department, and now employs over half a million career workers — name this agency?

United States Postal Service (USPS; also known as the Post Office, U.S. Mail, or simply the Postal Service) is an independent agency of the executive branch of the United States federal government responsible for providing postal service in the United States.

Warren G. Harding (November 2, 1865 - August 2, 1923) was the 29th president of the United States, serving from 1921 until his death in 1923.
This Israeli military officer commanded an elite unit during the daring 1976 raid that freed hostages held by hijackers at a Ugandan airport — who was he?
Yonatan Netanyahu (March 13, 1946 - July 4, 1976) was an Israeli military officer who commanded Sayeret Matkal during the Entebbe raid.
Educated at Sandhurst and Oxford, this monarch reigned as King of Malaysia from 2019 to 2024 while also serving as a Malaysian state's sixth sultan — who is he?
Abdullah of Pahang: King of Malaysia from 2019 to 2024. Abdullah became Sultan of Pahang upon his father's abdication in January 2019 who later died in May 2019.

Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani: President of Iran from 1989 to 1997. Rafsanjani became President of Iran after winning the 1989 election.

Benito Mussolini: Dictator of Italy from 1922 to 1943.

Boshin War: 1868–1869 Japanese civil war. When the Boshin War began, Japan was already modernizing, following the same course of advancement as that of the industrialized Western nations.
Cursed by Apollo to speak true prophecies that no one would ever believe, this Trojan priestess survived the fall of Troy only to be murdered alongside Agamemnon. Who was she?
Cassandra: Mythological prophetess and princess of Troy.

Chris McCandless: American hiker and explorer (1968–1992)

Continuation War: Finnish war against the Soviet Union (1941–44)

David Livingstone: British colonialist and missionary.

Domingo Faustino Sarmiento: President of Argentina from 1868 to 1874. Domingo Faustino Sarmiento (15 February 1811 – 11 September 1888) was President of Argentina from 1868 to 1874.

Ferdinand Marcos: President of the Philippines from 1965 to 1986.

French Consulate: Government of France from 1799 to 1804.
A Royal Navy officer charted the Pacific coast from California up to Alaska so thoroughly that an island, a major city, and a mountain all bear his name — who was he?

Coined by a 12th-century historian, this term describes Anglo-Saxon England's traditional division into seven petty kingdoms like Wessex, Mercia, and Kent — what's the term?
Heptarchy: Seven kingdoms of Anglo-Saxon England. The number of kingdoms and sub-kingdoms fluctuated rapidly during this period as competing kings contended for supremacy.
Officially known as Ansar Allah, this Zaydi Shia movement emerged in Yemen in the 1990s and is now backed by Iran as part of the 'Axis of Resistance.' Which group is this?
Houthis: Shia Islamist organization in Yemen.

Indian National Congress: Political party in India.
Later renamed Israel, this Hebrew patriarch tricked his aging father into blessing him instead of his twin brother Esau, and eventually followed his son Joseph's path into Egypt — who is he?
Jacob: Biblical patriarch, son of Isaac.

Born in Egypt as Hossam Boutros, this French far-right economist and media personality became spokesman for the National Front's Horaces group before later joining Éric Zemmour's Reconquête party. Who is he?
Jean Messiha: French media personality, former politician and civil servant (born 1970)
A Founding Father who signed the Treaty of Paris and directed U.S. foreign policy through much of the 1780s, he became the very first chief justice of the United States in 1789 — who was he?

Julia Gillard: Prime Minister of Australia from 2010 to 2013. Julia Eileen Gillard (born 29 September 1961) is an Australian former politician who served as the 27th prime minister of Australia from 2010 to 2013.
Rebranded in 2013 from a company once called Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, this Paris-based luxury conglomerate owns Gucci, Balenciaga, and Alexander McQueen — which company?

Slain by Heracles as the second of his Twelve Labours, this many-headed serpent grew back two heads for every one that was cut off — which mythical monster?
Lernaean Hydra: Snake-monster in Greek and Roman mythology.

Lucius Tarquinius Superbus: Seventh and last king of Rome.
The first woman to serve as chief minister of West Bengal, this politician also became the first sitting Indian chief minister to argue a case before the Supreme Court — who is she?
Mamata Banerjee: Chief Minister of West Bengal from 2011 to 2026.

Wife of the first U.S. President and wife of a Founding Father (1731–1802), she served as the inaugural first lady, defining that role and setting precedents still observed today—though the title itself was not coined until after her death. Who was she?
Martha Washington: First Lady of the United States from 1789 to 1797.

Mito Kakizawa: Japanese politician. Mito Kakizawa (柿沢未途, Kakizawa Mito; born 21 January 1971) is a Japanese politician and former member of the House of Representatives.

Brought to power by a palace conspiracy at just 11 years old, this Ottoman sultan let his mother Kösem rule as regent before seizing absolute power and becoming known for his brutal methods — who was he?
Murad IV: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1623 to 1640.

Vietnam's paramount leader as head of the Communist Party's Secretariat, Politburo, and Central Military Commission, this conservative Marxist-Leninist also served as president from 2018 to 2021 — who was he?
Nguyễn Phú Trọng: Leader of Vietnam from 2011 to 2024.
This four-star general commanded the defense of Kyiv and led the 2022 Kharkiv counteroffensive before becoming commander-in-chief of Ukraine's armed forces in 2024 — who is he?
This historical region of northeastern Greater Iran became the political and cultural base of the Parni people and the Arsacid dynasty — lending its name to a famous empire. Which region?

Parthia: Historical region located in northeastern Iran. Parthia (Old Persian: 𐎱𐎼𐎰𐎺 Parθava; Parthian: 𐭐𐭓𐭕𐭅 Parθaw; Middle Persian: 𐭯𐭫𐭮𐭥𐭡𐭥 Pahlaw) is a historical region located in northeastern Greater Iran.
These seafaring Semitic traders sprang from the Bronze Age Canaanites and spread from Lebanon's coast all the way to Iberia, leaving thousands of inscriptions — what was their civilization called?

Purgatory: Religious belief of Christianity, primarily Catholicism.

The eldest son of a U.S. president assassinated in 1865, this lawyer was the only one of his parents' four children to live past 18, and later served as Secretary of War — who is he?
Robert Todd Lincoln: American lawyer and politician (1843–1926)

Using the alias Saitani Umetarō while hunted by shogunate forces, this low-ranking samurai from Tosa negotiated the alliance between rival domains that helped topple the Tokugawa Shogunate — who was he?
Sakamoto Ryōma: Japanese samurai and politician (1836–1867)
Sparked when Qing officials seized a British-registered ship called the Arrow in 1856, this conflict between Britain, France, and China forced the legalization of the drug trade — which conflict?
Second Opium War: 1856–1860 war between British–French forces and China.
In 1968 she became the first Black woman elected to the U.S. Congress, and in 1972 the first Black major-party presidential candidate — who was she?
Formed after the October Revolution of 1917 and dissolved in 1991, this Moscow-based superpower was the largest country on Earth by area — which one?
Soviet Union: Country in Eurasia from 1922 to 1991.

Theodore Roosevelt: President of the United States from 1901 to 1909.

Transnistrian War: 1990–1992 separatist conflict in Moldova. Cojocaru, the Moldovan defeat in this war directly led to implementation of Moldovan neutrality.
This Mexican revolutionary-turned-president oversaw the drafting of the 1917 constitution and kept his country neutral in World War I before being assassinated in 1920 — who is he?
Venustiano Carranza: President of Mexico from 1914 to 1920.

Wanrong: Empress of Manchukuo from 1934 to 1945 (1906–1946)
A descendant of the Viking Rollo and once called 'the Bastard,' this Duke of Normandy won the Battle of Hastings in 1066 and became the first Norman king of England — who was he?
William the Conqueror: King of England from 1066 to 1087.
Made by young Indonesians on 28 October 1928, this nationalist declaration proclaimed one motherland, one nation, and one unifying language — what is it called?
Youth Pledge: 1928 declaration by Indonesian nationalists.

Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which of these was founded earliest?
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Donna Strickland is a physicist. Donna Theo Strickland (born May 27, 1959) is a Canadian optical physicist and pioneer in the field of pulsed lasers.
Which of these is a chemist?
Carl Wilhelm Scheele is a chemist. Carl Wilhelm Scheele (German: [ˈʃeːlə], Swedish: [ˈɧêːlɛ]; 9 December 1742 – 21 May 1786) was a German-Swedish pharmaceutical chemist.
What is the atomic number of Oganesson?
Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
In what year was Pythagoras born?
Pythagoras: Pythagoras of Samos (Ancient Greek: Πυθαγόρας; c. 570 – c. 495 BC) was an ancient Ionian Greek philosopher, polymath, and the eponymous founder of Pythagoreanism.
In what year did Srinivasa Ramanujan die?
Srinivasa Ramanujan Iyengar (22 December 1887 – 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
In what year was Silicon discovered?
Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
Which company manufactures Antonov An-124 Ruslan?
Antonov An-124 Ruslan: Aviastar-SP. The An-124 remains the largest military transport aircraft in service.
In which country is Dassault Rafale based?
Dassault Rafale: France. Dassault built a technology demonstrator that first flew in July 1986 as part of an eight-year flight-test programme, paving the way for approval of the project.
Who is credited with discovering Horologium?

Horologium (constellation): Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. It was first described by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in 1756 and visualized by him as a clock with a pendulum and a second hand.
Who is credited with discovering Hubble's law?
Hubble's law: Georges Lemaître. The Friedmann equations showed the universe might be expanding, and presented the expansion speed if that were the case.
Who is credited with discovering Eris?
Eris (dwarf planet): Michael E. Brown. Eris (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
Hiding in coffee, fresh bread, and ripe fruit, this aldehyde is also what your liver makes when breaking down alcohol — and a prime culprit behind the morning-after hangover. What is it?
Acetaldehyde (IUPAC systematic name ethanal) is an organic chemical compound with the formula CH3CH=O.
This genus of more than 650 flowering succulent species includes a 'true' member cultivated worldwide as the standard source for a soothing pharmaceutical gel — what's the genus?
Aloe (also written Alo) is a genus containing over 650 species of flowering succulent plants.
Whether contracted through the skin, the lungs, or the gut, this Bacillus-driven infection can take up to two months to show symptoms — what is it?
Anthrax is an infection caused by the bacterium Bacillus anthracis or Bacillus cereus biovar anthracis.
This common vision condition occurs when the cornea or lens is slightly egg-shaped rather than spherical, causing blurred vision at any distance. What is it?
Astigmatism is a type of refractive error due to rotational asymmetry in the eye's refractive power.
This steel-gray, lightweight metal with atomic number 4 is found in gemstones like aquamarine and emerald, but within the cores of stars it gets destroyed as fast as it forms — what element is it?
Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
First described in 1903 from fossils found in Colorado, this sauropod dinosaur's Greek name means arm lizard, a reference to its proportionately long front limbs — what genus is it?
Brachiosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Jurassic, about 155.6 to 145.5 million years ago.
This group of diseases involves uncontrolled cell growth, includes over 100 types, and is responsible for about 33% of deaths when linked to tobacco and alcohol. What disease are we discussing?
Cancer is a group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth typically resulting in tumors with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body.
Also known by the taxonomic synonym Epilobium, this hardy perennial in the willowherb family is native throughout the temperate north — which plant?
Chamaenerion angustifolium is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the willowherb family, Onagraceae.
This neurological disorder strikes one side of the head around the eye and temple, often at the very same hour each day for an 8-to-10-week stretch before vanishing for months — what condition is it?
Cluster headache is a neurological disorder characterized by episodes of severe headaches on one side of the head, typically around the eye and temple, lasting between 15 minutes to three hours.
Native to Europe and Western Asia, this birch-family shrub produces the round nuts sold commercially as hazelnuts — which species?
Corylus avellana is a species of flowering plant in the birch family Betulaceae.

This common cough suppressant found in cold medicine was combined with bupropion in 2022 to create a fast-acting antidepressant, despite belonging to the same chemical class as morphine — what drug is it?
Dextromethorphan is a cough suppressant used in many cough and cold medicines.
Named from Greek roots meaning 'to repeat' and 'speech,' this automatic repetition of another person's vocalizations is closely related to echopraxia, the repeating of movements. What is it called?
Echolalia is the repetition of vocalizations made by another person; when repeated by the same person, it is called palilalia.
This American physicist won a Nobel Prize for inventing a particle accelerator and later worked on uranium-isotope separation for the Manhattan Project. Who is he?
Ernest Lawrence (August 8, 1901 - August 27, 1958) was an American physicist who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1939 for his invention of the cyclotron.
This body part is a prominent, usually flexible digit found on the forelimbs of most four-limbed vertebrates — on the hind limbs, the equivalent shorter digits are instead called toes. What is it?
Finger is a prominent digit on the forelimbs of most tetrapod vertebrate animals, especially those with prehensile extremities (i.e.
First studied scientifically by an Augustinian friar experimenting with pea plants in 19th-century Brno, this branch of biology examines heredity and trait inheritance — which field?
Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
In this rapid-onset condition the immune system attacks the peripheral nerves, so weakness creeps up from the feet and hands — and about 15% of patients need a ventilator. What is it?
Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rapid-onset muscle weakness caused by the immune system damaging the peripheral nervous system.

The reciprocal cross to the more common mule, this equine hybrid is the offspring of a male horse and a female donkey, differing from its counterpart in both physiology and temperament — what is it called?
Hinny is a domestic equine hybrid, the offspring of a male horse (a stallion) and a female donkey (a jenny).

This phenomenon describes how a system's state depends on its history, as when a magnet holds different moments depending on past field changes — it underlies memory in a hard disk drive. What is it called?
Hysteresis is the dependence of the state of a system on its history. Hysteresis can be found in physics, chemistry, engineering, biology, and economics.

This American physicist worked on the Manhattan Project, then in 1949 proposed that — contrary to belief — not all atomic nuclei are spherical, an idea Aage Bohr later helped confirm. Who won a share of the 1975 Nobel for it?
James Rainwater (December 9, 1917 - May 31, 1986) was an American physicist who shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1975 for his part in determining the asymmetrical shapes of certain atomic nuclei.
Linked to a herpesvirus and immune suppression, this cancer causing purple skin lesions was already being described by Hippocrates in the 300s BC — which condition?
Kaposi's sarcoma (KS) is a type of cancer that can form masses on the skin, in lymph nodes, in the mouth, or in other organs.
Representing the Nemean Lion slain by Heracles as one of his twelve labors, this zodiac constellation sits between Cancer and Virgo — which constellation?
Leo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac, between Cancer, the Crab, to the west and Virgo, the Maiden, to the east.
Credited as the 'Father of Cinematography' for filming Roundhay Garden Scene in Leeds in 1888, this French inventor mysteriously vanished in 1890 before cinema took off — who was he?

Louis Le Prince (28 August 1841 - disappeared 16 September 1890; declared dead 16 September 1897) was a French artist and the inventor of an early motion-picture camera, and director of Roundhay Garden Scene.
This Italian economist served as prime minister from 2021 to 2022 after previously heading the European Central Bank for eight years and the Bank of Italy before that — who is he?

Mario Draghi (born 3 September 1947) is an Italian politician, economist, academic, banker, statesman, and civil servant, who served as the prime minister of Italy from 13 February 2021 to 22 October 2022.
This medical condition is diagnosed when the erect length of the affected organ measures at least two and a half standard deviations below the average size for age — what condition is it?
Micropenis is an unusually small penis.
With shells that are elongated and wedge-shaped rather than round, these bivalves attach themselves to shorelines using threads nicknamed a "beard" — what are they?
Mussel is the common name used for members of several families of bivalve molluscs, from saltwater and freshwater habitats.
Catalyzed in nature by iron-bearing nitrogenase enzymes and famously partnered with legumes, this process turns molecular N2 into ammonia — what's it called?
Nitrogen fixation is a chemical process by which molecular dinitrogen (N2) is converted into ammonia (NH3).
All 14 species of this slim-bodied, dense-furred mammal are semiaquatic, and they're famous for playful antics like sliding into the water and juggling stones — what is it?
Otter are carnivorous mammals in the subfamily Lutrinae.
It comes in a G version for the needle and a V version for the mouth, and it owes its name to the very mould it's coaxed from — which medication?
Penicillin (PCN or PEN) are a group of beta-lactam antibiotics originally obtained from Penicillium moulds, principally P. chrysogenum.
This scientific term for a group of fin-footed, mostly marine mammals includes walruses, sea lions, fur seals, and true earless seals — 34 living species in all. What is the term?
Pinniped are a widely distributed and diverse clade of carnivorous, fin-footed, semiaquatic, mostly marine mammals.
Bloating, mood swings, breast tenderness and irritability that flare in the week or two before menstruation and fade once bleeding begins — what disruptive condition is this?
Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a disruptive set of emotional and physical symptoms that regularly occur in the one to two weeks before the start of each menstrual period.

Named for the ragged appearance of its leaves, this genus of flowering plants native mainly to North America has become an invasive nuisance in parts of Europe due to climate change — what plant is it?
Ragweed are flowering plants in the genus Ambrosia in the aster family, Asteraceae.

This long-term skin condition causes facial redness, pimples, and swelling, and can lead to a severely enlarged, reddened nose in extreme cases — its exact cause remains unknown — name this condition?
Rosacea is a long-term skin condition that typically affects the face.
About 950 species of these spiny, globe-shaped marine animals crawl the seabed on tube feet, found from tide pools down to 5,000 metres deep. What are they?
Sea urchin are the class Echinoidea within the echinoderms.
Pythons and boas of this limbless reptile group still carry a tiny pelvic girdle and vestigial leg-stubs near the cloaca, hinting at long-lost legs. What animal is this?
Snake are elongated legless reptiles of the suborder Serpentes.
A small Eurasian mustelid that turns brilliant white in winter, this animal's coat — known as ermine — once draped Catholic monarchs and the Infant Jesus of Prague — what is it?
Stoat (Mustela erminea), also known as the Eurasian ermine or ermine, is a species of mustelid native to Eurasia and the northern regions of North America.
Named for a U.S. state where its discovery research was based, this synthetic element (symbol Ts) holds the second-highest atomic number of all and was the most recently discovered — what is it?
Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.

This parasite can infect nearly any warm-blooded animal, but can only sexually reproduce inside cats, and is famous for altering infected rodents' behavior to make them less afraid of feline predators — what parasite is it?
Toxoplasma gondii is a species of parasitic alveolate that causes toxoplasmosis.
Just 25 light-years away, this is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra and the fifth-brightest star in the entire night sky — what is it?
Vega is the brightest star in the northern constellation of Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr.
Chairman of the Polish People's Party since 2015 and a former Minister of Labour and Social Affairs, this physician-turned-politician ran for the Polish presidency in 2020 — who is he?
Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (born 10 August 1981) is a Polish physician and politician, who has served as the Deputy Prime Minister of Poland, and Minister of National Defence since 2023.
Named for the skull-shaped marking on its thorax and first classified by Carl Linnaeus in 1758, this large moth was immortalized on the poster for 'The Silence of the Lambs' — which insect?
Acherontia atropos: Species of moth. It is most commonly identified by the vaguely skull-shaped pattern adorning the thorax, the characteristic from which its common and scientific names are derived.
Scientifically named Gadus chalcogrammus, this schooling member of the cod family gathers in massive numbers in the eastern Bering Sea — which fish?
Alaska pollock: Species of fish. The Alaska pollock also known as Pacific pollock or walleye pollock (Gadus chalcogrammus) is a marine fish species of the cod genus Gadus and family Gadidae.
Native to the Americas, this plant is better known by its common names common ragweed, annual ragweed, or low ragweed — what is its scientific name?
Ambrosia artemisiifolia: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family.
First described by a German entomologist in 1818 and known as the 'marsh mosquito,' this genus is the only one that transmits malaria to humans — which genus is it?
Anopheles: Genus of mosquito. The genus Anopheles diverged from other mosquitoes approximately 100 million years ago (mya), and, like other mosquitoes, the eggs, larvae, and pupae are aquatic.
The third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere at nearly 1%, this noble gas takes its name from an Ancient Greek word meaning 'lazy' or 'inactive' — what element is it?
Argon: Chemical element with atomic number 18 (Ar)
Native to the Americas and prized for thousands of years for its unusually oily fruit, this evergreen of the laurel family bears what's botanically a giant berry around a single seed — what is it?
Avocado: Species of flowering plant in the laurel family.
Nicknamed 'top shelf' dizziness, this inner-ear disorder causes brief spinning sensations lasting under a minute whenever you tilt or turn your head — what is this condition called?
Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo: Medical condition. Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), sometimes called "top shelf vertigo", is a disorder arising from a problem in the inner ear.
Composed of plasma plus red cells, white cells, and platelets, this circulatory fluid delivers oxygen and nutrients to the body while carrying away waste — what is it?
Blood: Body fluid in the circulatory system. Plasma, which constitutes 55% of blood fluid, is mostly water (92% by volume), and contains proteins, glucose, mineral ions, and hormones.
Grown on one of the Amazon's largest and longest-lived trees, this selenium-rich edible seed comes in a shell weighing up to 2 kilograms combined with its fruit. What is it?
Brazil nut: Species of tree and its edible seeds.
This intensely sour citrus hybrid — a cross between a kumquat and likely a mandarin orange — is a staple of Philippine cooking and also popular in Malaysian and Indonesian cuisine — which fruit?
Calamansi: Hybrid species of citrus. Calamansi (Citrus × microcarpa), also known as calamondin, Philippine lime, or Philippine lemon, is a citrus hybrid cultivated predominantly in the Philippines.
Extracted from the cochineal insect, this bright-red pigment is also known by the food-additive code E120 — what is it called?
Carmine: Pigment, aluminium salt of carminic acid.
The biochemist hailed as the "father" of industrial fermentation, instrumental in the 1917 Balfour Declaration, became the first president of Israel — who was he?
Chaim Weizmann: Israeli statesman and British chemist (1874–1952)

Native to Sri Lanka, the inner bark of this evergreen tree is the original source of a beloved baking spice, sometimes distinguished from a cheaper cousin as the 'true' or 'Ceylon' variety — which tree?
Cinnamomum verum: Species of tree. The inner bark of the tree is historically regarded as the spice cinnamon, though this term was later generalized to include C. cassia as well.
Also known as foremilk or historically as 'beestings,' this early substance produced by mammary glands right after birth delivers antibodies and immune factors to newborns. What is it?
Colostrum: Form of milk produced immediately following the delivery of newborn.
First described in 1880 by a French neurologist, this rare delusion convinces sufferers that they are dead, don't exist, or have lost their internal organs — what is it called?
Cotard's syndrome: Delusion that one is dead or non-existent.
Bred in Germany with short legs and a long body to chase badgers into their burrows, which hound breed comes in smooth-, wire-, and long-haired varieties?

Historically defined by having two embryonic seed leaves, this once-standard division of flowering plants covers around 200,000 species but turned out not to share one common ancestor — which plant group?
Dicotyledon: Historical grouping of flowering plants.
This first section of the small intestine, often the principal site of iron absorption, connects the stomach to the middle portion of the intestine — what is it?
Duodenum: First section of the small intestine. The duodenum is the first section of the small intestine in most vertebrates, including mammals, reptiles, and birds.
A Swedish scientist and inventor until, at 53, dreams and visions sent him into a spiritual phase, this polymath became best known for his 1758 book on the afterlife, Heaven and Hell — who was he?
Emanuel Swedenborg: Swedish scientist, philosopher, and theologian (1688–1772)
With a sweet smell like pear drops, this colorless solvent turns up in nail-polish remover and is used to decaffeinate tea and coffee. What is it?
Named after a 19th-century English physicist, this SI unit measures a material's ability to store electrical charge, equal to one coulomb per volt — what is it?
Farad: SI unit of electric capacitance.
Patented in 1962 and sold under a brand name synonymous with 'roofies,' this benzodiazepine is notoriously linked to date-rape drug use — what is it?
Flunitrazepam: Benzodiazepine sedative. Flunitrazepam, sold under the brand name Rohypnol among others, is a benzodiazepine used to treat severe insomnia and assist with anesthesia.
Born in Pisa in 1564, this Italian polymath has been crowned the father of observational astronomy and the scientific method — and was among the earliest tinkerers to build a thermoscope. Who is he?
Galileo Galilei: Italian physicist and astronomer (1564–1642)

This Italian friar and cosmological theorist proposed that stars were distant suns with their own planets, and was tried for heresy by the Roman Inquisition for insisting the universe is infinite — who was he?
Giordano Bruno: Italian Dominican friar, philosopher and mathematician (1548–1600)

Once classified as a subfamily of the seabasses, this diverse family of marine ray-finned fish is now treated as distinct, with most members drawn from two large genera. What are they commonly called?
Grouper: Family of fishes. The common name "grouper" is usually given to fish in one of two large genera: Epinephelus and Mycteroperca.
Spiny like a porcupine but actually a distant cousin of the shrew, this nocturnal little mammal comes in 17 species across Europe, Asia, and Africa — and was introduced to New Zealand; what is it?
Known as the great apes, this primate family holds eight living species across four genera — orangutans, gorillas, chimps and bonobos, plus one more: us. What is it?
Hominidae: Family of primates. The original meaning of "hominid" referred only to humans (Homo) and their closest extinct relatives.

Responsible for nearly half a million deaths each year, this condition occurs when the body produces or absorbs more heat than it can dissipate, most often from heat stroke or a drug reaction — what condition?
Hyperthermia: Elevated body temperature due to failed thermoregulation.
Covering patents, copyrights, trademarks, and trade secrets, this legal category of intangible creations first developed as a concept in 17th- and 18th-century England — what is it called?
Intellectual property: Ownership of creative expressions and processes.
He won the Fields Medal in 1954 and, nearly half a century later, the very first Abel Prize in 2003 — which French mathematician of algebraic topology and geometry is it?

Conceived as a high-speed 'Schnellbomber' for the German Luftwaffe, this twin-engined WWII aircraft evolved into everything from a night fighter to the explosive lower half of composite 'Mistel' combinations — what is it?
Junkers Ju 88: German twin-engined multirole combat aircraft.

Until a 2020 taxonomic overhaul split many of its 261 species into 25 new genera, this rod-shaped, gram-positive bacterial genus formed a major part of the human gut and vaginal microbiota — what genus?
Lactobacillus: Genus of bacteria. Lactobacillus forms biofilms in the vaginal and gut microbiota, allowing them to persist in harsh environmental conditions and maintain ample populations.
This fibrous connective tissue links bone to bone in every one of the 30,000 known amniote species, and in birds it even anchors flight feathers to bone — what is it?

With nearly 5,000 species, these wingless parasitic insects spend their whole lives on a single warm-blooded host, either chewing skin and feathers or piercing the skin to feed on blood — what are they?
Louse: Infraorder of insects. Louse (pl.: lice) is the common name for any member of the infraorder Phthiraptera, which contains nearly 5,000 species of wingless parasitic insects.
Nicknamed the 'tree of death' and 'beach apple,' this small-fruited tropical tree oozes a milky sap so toxic it can blister skin on contact — which tree?
Manchineel: Poisonous plant from tropical North and South America.
This small, highly social mongoose from southern Africa lives in packs of up to 30, with a dominance hierarchy where usually only the top pair breeds. What animal is it?
Meerkat: Species of mongoose from Southern Africa. The meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.

This medical condition, usually diagnosed shortly after birth, is defined as a length at least 2.5 standard deviations below the average and affects about 1.5 in 10,000 male newborns in North America. What is this condition?
This rounded mound of fatty tissue overlies the junction where the two pubic bones meet — what is it?
Mons pubis: Rounded mass of fatty tissue found over the pubic symphysis.

The first production helicopter with fully fly-by-wire flight controls, this European twin-engine military chopper comes in troop-transport and naval anti-submarine variants flown by over a dozen NATO nations. What is it?
NHIndustries NH90: Family of military helicopters.
Surrounded by a typically darker-colored areola, this raised region of breast tissue is where milk exits through the lactiferous ducts during lactation — what is it?
Nipple: Part of the breast. The milk can flow through the nipple passively, or it can be ejected by smooth muscle contractions that occur along with the ductal system.
Sold under the brand name Prilosec, this proton-pump inhibitor treats acid reflux and peptic ulcers — what is it?
Omeprazole: Medication to treat gastroesophageal reflux disease and other conditions.
Located behind the stomach, this gland is 99 percent exocrine yet still secretes insulin and glucagon to regulate blood sugar — which organ?
Pancreas: Organ of the digestive system and endocrine system of vertebrates.
Harvested from Penicillium moulds and brewed in deep tanks, this β-lactam was among the first medicines to knock out staph and strep infections. What is it?
Penicillin: Group of antibiotics derived from fungi.
Enclosed in a papery husk derived from its calyx, this nightshade genus includes the tomatillo and Cape gooseberry among its edible-fruited species — which genus?
Most commonly referring to a type called PET, this category of polymers built from ester linkages is often blended with cotton to reduce wrinkling — what is it called?
Polyester: Category of polymers, in which the monomers are joined together by ester links.
This deciduous member of the rose family includes many varieties known as plums in English, with greengages and damsons among its subspecies — which species is it?
Prunus domestica: Species of flowering plant.

Historically nicknamed 'hydrophobia' because sufferers panic at the offer of a drink, this viral disease causes severe brain inflammation and is virtually always fatal once symptoms appear. What is it?
Rabies: Deadly viral disease, transmitted through animals.
Nicknamed golden root or Arctic root, this Crassulaceae plant is popular in herbal supplements even though the FDA has warned sellers against overselling its health benefits — which plant?
Rhodiola rosea: Species of flowering plant in the stonecrop family.
Extremely cold-hardy and thriving in poor soil, this cereal grass is a staple grain behind Scandinavian crispbread and a certain whiskey style — what is it?
Rye: Species of grain. Rye (Secale cereale) is a grass grown extensively as a grain, a cover crop and a forage crop.
Sitting near the center of the Milky Way between Libra and Sagittarius, this zodiac constellation's recognition predates ancient Greek culture — which constellation?
Scorpius: Zodiac constellation in the southern celestial hemisphere.
In this inherited blood disorder, faulty haemoglobin warps red cells into a rigid crescent shape that can't bend through capillaries, causing painful blockages — what is it?
Also nicknamed 'sour dock,' this perennial herb native to Eurasia is often eaten as a tangy leaf vegetable in grassland habitats — which plant?
Sorrel: Flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae.
In this eye disorder, the two eyes fail to align properly on the same object, which can cause a lazy eye and lost depth perception if it persists through much of childhood. What condition is it?
Strabismus: Eyes not aligning when looking at something.
Named by Linnaeus in 1753 but called cempōhualxōchitl by the Nahua long before, this genus of Mexican-native flowers is commonly known as marigolds — what's the genus?
A cousin of caffeine found in trace amounts in tea, coffee, and chocolate, which methylxanthine drug is used to treat asthma and COPD by blocking adenosine receptors?
Theophylline: Drug used to treat respiratory diseases.
This central part of the body, from which the head, neck, limbs, and tail extend, is divided into chest, abdomen, and pelvic segments — which body part?

Torso: Central part of the living body. The tetrapod torso — including that of a human — can be divided into segments:

The chest or upper torso.

A reddish-purple natural dye secreted by sea snails in the Muricidae family, also called royal purple or imperial dye. The colored compound is 6,6'-dibromoindigo, extracted from snails like Bolinus brandaris. What is this ancient dye?
Tyrian purple: Natural dye extracted from Murex sea snails. The name Tyrian refers to the city of Tyre in ancient Phoenicia (modern-day Lebanon).

The northernmost marsupial on Earth, this cat-sized nocturnal opportunist is a familiar visitor to trash cans and compost piles across North America, and often ends up as roadkill due to its slow pace — what is it?
Virginia opossum: Species of North American marsupial.
This American child prodigy entered Harvard at 11 and lectured on four-dimensional geometry at 12 before deliberately retreating from public life — who was he?
William James Sidis: American mathematician, polyglot, and child prodigy (1898–1944)
Iron is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for iron is Fe. Iron is a chemical element; it has symbol Fe and atomic number 26.
Plutonium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for plutonium is Pu. Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
